name: auth
description: Identity, capabilities and delegation: who you are, what you may do, and how to grant bounded authority to others via UCAN tokens. Load when permissions matter.

content.inline:
## Auth & capabilities
Identity is a DID; every job records its caller. `v/ops/auth/whoami` returns yours.

Capabilities are `{with, can}` pairs: `with` is a resource (a path prefix like `w/reports/`, a DID URL, or a scheme resource); `can` is an ability. Core abilities: `crud/read`, `crud/write`, `asset/read`, `asset/store`, `invoke` (the right to run compute/external ops — scopable to op-path prefixes), plus adapter-specific ones (`mcp/manage`, `sql/query`...). Enforcement happens at each operation's own enforcement point — a denial reads `Capability denied` and names the resource.

An agent's inherent capabilities are its `config.caps`. Presented UCANs are further positive grants: grant sources combine with OR semantics, so any one covering grant authorises an action. Anonymous callers get read-only (`crud/read` on their own namespace + `asset/read`).

Delegation (UCAN):
- issue `{aud, att, exp}` — a venue-signed token granting the audience DID the attenuated capabilities `att` (an array of `{with, can}`) until `exp`. Grant the MINIMUM: narrow resources, short expiry.
- verify `{token, with?, can?, aud?}` checks a presented token.
- Callers present tokens in the request envelope (`ucans`); cross-user reads then verify against them.

Loading a skill never grants authority — its tools are still checked against all capabilities available for that invocation.
